subject: Skyline: request for service-remedy & latency SLO exception / approval needed
messages:
From: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@skyline.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@skyline.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service remedies / latency SLOs – request for non-standard terms

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Skyline is excited about Redwood’s latency profile, but a couple of items came up during procurement and security review that we need to resolve before legal signs off.

High-level ask: we need an exception to the standard Remedy table and Latency SLO thresholds in the hosted Customer Agreement for our Enterprise plan. Specifically:
- Uptime target: we need 99.99% for our public API endpoints (you currently list 99.95%).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency must be <= 120ms for our production region during normal load.
- Credits/remedy cap: procurement insists on a fixed service-credit cap (no more than 5% monthly credit) rather than the standard sliding scale.

We understand these are non-standard. In return Skyline is prepared to commit to a 24-month reserved capacity and provide a case study and reference after go-live. Procurement also asked whether Redwood can offer a one-time onboarding discount off the first 3 months of committed spend — they proposed 10%.

I’ve attached Skyline_Service_Technical_SLOs.pdf with the specific endpoints and traffic profiles. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the uptime and latency exceptions and the fixed-credit cap? If not, what mitigations or alternative remedies do you recommend?

Best,
Rachel Stern
Senior Procurement Manager
Skyline, Inc.
Attachments: Skyline_Service_Technical_SLOs.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@skyline.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@skyline.com>, logan.wright@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service remedies / latency SLOs – request for non-standard terms

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attached profile. I looped in Logan (VP, Sales) and Lauren (Head of Legal) to evaluate the requests. Quick thoughts up front:

- Uptime: 99.99% is above our standard hosted SLA for the entry enterprise tier; we can consider 99.95 with a path to 99.99 for Dedicated pools (reserved instances in a single region) pending capacity commitment.
- Latency: 120ms p95 is aggressive but may be achievable with Dedicated pools + affinity routing and an SLO carveout for warm KV-cached requests. We need to validate against the traffic profiles you shared.
- Credit cap: we can discuss a firm monthly cap; Finance will want to model worst-case exposure.

I’ve attached our initial redline request doc (Skyline_Requested_Redlines.docx) — it lists options we can offer. Can we schedule a 30-min call this week with procurement and our engineering lead to walk the traffic profile and confirm where Dedicated makes sense?

Also, Skyline, if you can confirm committed baseline (monthly spend) for the reserved pool, that will help speed an approval decision.

Thanks — looping Logan and Lauren for exec/legal guidance.

—Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: Skyline_Requested_Redlines.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: francesca.mills@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Skyline: request for service-remedy & latency SLO exception / approval needed

Hi Logan / Lauren —

FWD of the procurement ask from Skyline. TL;DR summary + asks for approval: 

Summary of Skyline asks:
- 99.99% uptime for public endpoints (they’re willing to commit to 24 months reserved capacity).
- Latency p95 <= 120ms for production region.
- Fixed monthly service-credit cap at 5%.
- One-time 10% onboarding discount for first 3 months of committed baseline (they proposed 10%).

Our recommended options (from ops/eng & deal desk):
1) Offer Dedicated pool (reserved) in primary region with a target SLA of 99.95 for hosted, upgrade path to 99.99 for Dedicated once provisioning and baseline committed is validated.
2) For latency, include a carveout: p95 <= 120ms for cached/pinned routes otherwise standard p95 applies; we can add a performance onboarding period (30 days) where we tune kernels/routing.
3) Approve a fixed credit cap of 5% monthly (legal will want specific language limiting "systemic" events; finance wants an overall annual exposure cap).
4) Approve a one-time onboarding discount of 10% for first 3 months contingent on signed 24-month reserved commitment and a minimum monthly spend threshold.

Asks: 
- Logan: can you sign off on the commercial concessions (10% onboarding + acceptance of credit cap) so I can move this through DocuSign?
- Lauren: please propose redline language that limits the remedy exposure (suggest: annual credit cap = min(12 * monthly fee * 5%, fixed-dollar cap to be determined by Finance)) and confirm whether the Dedicated upgrade path wording is acceptable.

I’ve attached the redlines and Skyline’s SLO profile again. This is a good strategic customer and reference. Appreciate quick turnaround — Skyline procurement is pacing this tightly and is expecting contract language by EOD Friday.

—Vanessa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, finance-approvals@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Skyline: request for service-remedy & latency SLO exception / approval needed

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Approve moving forward with the approach below, subject to Legal drafting protective language and Finance confirming the numeric cap:

Approved commercial concessions:
- One-time onboarding discount: 10% off the first 3 months of committed baseline, conditional on a 24-month reserved commitment and a minimum monthly spend of $75k.
- Service-credit cap: agree to a 5% monthly credit cap, with Legal to add an annual exposure ceiling (Finance to propose the absolute dollar cap; finance-approvals has been CC'd).
- Uptime: do NOT commit to 99.99 on hosted. Offer 99.95 hosted and 99.99 for Dedicated pools after provisioning validation (we’ll include a 30-day performance tuning window).
- Latency: accept proposed carveout for pinned/cached routes; Legal to include a definition of "cached/pinned routes" and an onboarding tuning period.

Next steps:
- Lauren: please prepare final redline including the annual exposure limit language and the Dedicated upgrade clause.
- Vanessa: get DocuSign packet ready but hold signature until Legal completes redlines and Finance confirms the absolute dollar cap.

This is strategically important — prioritize.

—Logan Wright
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
